I first want to acknowledge the difficulties of finding speakers week after week, i'm sure a lot of work goes into it with lots of criteria including diversity. So i'm hoping it is a constructive feedback.

I find that speakers are a lot less engaging if they are online but also not even in Canada. In the presentation, there was a lot of reference to Chicago, and i had a lot of difficulties relating it to how it would apply to Toronto or even Canada (even if in general housing is a universal topic). It's already difficult to keep a room engaged when the speaker is 100% remote, but when we add to the fact the talk isn't having a strong link to Toronto, this made the talk hard to listen to.

Few weeks back with the talk with Eugene Chen, even if he was from Calgary, I found that at least it was relating a lot more to our reality in Toronto, how the election tool could be used in Toronto (with actual screenshots in Toronto), how the speaker itself is part of Civic Tech Canada and would be visiting Toronto, etc. But a 100% remote speaker with no tie or no link to Canada in their project, i find we are steering away of CivicTech Toronto and our local realities.  

Again thank you on all the work you've been doing finding speakers, just a feedback I wanted to relay.
